name: runbook-cert-check
description: Certificate check for every TLS endpoint in the inventory (expired, expiring within the warning days, self-signed, name mismatch, chain), and - when one needs renewing and the renewal is known (certbot, an ACME client, a documented command) - approval, renewal, and a TLS probe to verify.

warn_days.description: Warn when fewer days are left.

renew.description: true when a certificate needs renewing and the renewal command is known

check.title: Check certificates
check.prompt:
Probe the certificate of every service with a TLS endpoint in the inventory (ops_inventory list services; probe type tls, warn_days {{input.warn_days}}), and any https health URL. Write .harness/ops/reports/certificates.md: per endpoint the subject, issuer, expiry, days left and problems. For each one that needs renewing, find how it is renewed on its host with read-only commands (certbot certificates, ls /etc/letsencrypt/renewal, the service's documentation in the workspace) and give the exact renewal command; if it cannot be found, say who must renew it.

Report: the endpoints with days left and problems; renew is true only when a renewal is due AND its exact command is known.

approve.title: Approve the renewal
approve.message:
Renew these certificates with the commands below?

{{state.check}}

renew-certs.title: Renew
renew-certs.prompt:
A person approved renewing the certificates in .harness/ops/reports/certificates.md. Run exactly the renewal commands listed there (ssh_exec as: "operator"), and reload the service only if the command does not (as listed).

Report: each command and its result.

verify.title: Verify
verify.prompt:
Probe (type tls) every renewed endpoint again: VERIFIED when each now has at least {{input.warn_days}} days left and no problems; otherwise FAILED.

Report: the new expiry dates.
